paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. David is a king, a giant-killer, a man who once faced Goliath, and in 2 Samuel 21:15 the Bible says plainly that he "became exhausted." Nobody is too strong to run out of strength. Honestly, that's the most comforting thing I've heard all week, because I run out of steam pressing ONE tray of dough.

Now look at what happens when David is spent. Abishai comes to his aid, and David's men say they want to keep "the lamp of Israel" from being "extinguished" (2 Samuel 21:17). Then the passage keeps going, and Sibbecai, Elhanan and Jonathan each take on a descendant of Rapha (2 Samuel 21:18-21). Four fell "at the hands of David and his servants" (2 Samuel 21:22). That's the lesson: the work gets done by a whole team, and you don't have to carry it all alone.

So here's the big idea, baker. When you're worn out, the answer isn't to pretend you're not. Let somebody step in, and be glad to step in for somebody else when it's their turn. Nobody in this passage is the hero all by himself, and I think that is exactly how it was meant to be.
